Group=1 ist also die Interventionsgruppe (EX), nicht die Kontrollgruppe. arm_control sollte '2' sein, nicht '1'. control_arm_matches daher 'no'. 3) covars_published in der Registry-Zeile listet 'Age,BMI'; im publizierten Statistical-Analysis-Abschnitt werden Age/BMI aber nicht als Kovariaten in ein Modell aufgenommen, sondern nur deskriptiv per unabhaengigem t-Test auf Baseline-Vergleichbarkeit geprueft (Table 3). Die publizierte Primaeranalyse (Mixed-ANOVA) ist unadjustiert. 4) Die Outcome-Variable Post.Strenth.R.Ext/Pre.Strenth.R.Ext (rechtes Bein) entspricht inhaltlich der in Table 4 berichteten Zeile 'Knee extensors' (Pre/Post-Mittelwerte in den Rohdaten stimmen exakt mit Table 3/4 ueberein), sodass zumindest die Variablenzuordnung selbst korrekt ist - nur die Auswahl als 'primaeres' Outcome und arm_control sind falsch/irrefuehrend.

primary_outcome: One-repetition maximum (1RM) in the free-weight back squat (chronic adaptation)
primary_timepoint: post-intervention (after the 6-week training programme), compared with pre-intervention baseline
registry_issues: The paper never labels ONE single outcome as 'the primary outcome' for the whole trial, and it explicitly has two separate domains (acute, single-session; chronic, 6-week pre/post). (1) The strongest signal of an intended primary outcome is the a-priori G*Power sample-size calculation, which was computed specifically 'for changes in one-repetition maximum (1RM)... with two groups and two time points (pre- and post-intervention)' (Section 2.1, p.2) -- i.e. 1RM, not CMJ, and this matches the chronic/post-intervention timeframe our registry's primary_time='post' points to. 1RM is also literally first-named among the chronic adaptation outcomes both in the abstract ('Chronic adaptations included one-repetition maximum (1RM), relative isometric peak force, muscle endurance, CMJ height, velocity at 70% 1RM (v70)...') and in Methods 2.4.4, and is analysed first in Results 3.2. CMJ height is listed 4th of 5 chronic outcomes and its chronic result was explicitly null ('Neither protocol improved CMJ height', Discussion p.9; no significant pairwise differences after Holm correction, Results 3.2). So CMJ_mean is NOT well supported as this study's primary outcome. (2) Separately and confusingly, the word 'primary' IS used explicitly in Methods, but only for a distinct set of ACUTE within-session fatigue outcomes: 'LMMs were fitted for each primary fatigue-related outcome (MPV, VL, changes in CMJ and RSI mod.)...' (Section 2.4.3, p.4). This 'CMJ' is the acute pre-to-post-set jump-height CHANGE recorded after each of the 12 training sessions (Fatigue sheet: CMJ_pre_mean/CMJ_post_mean per session), a conceptually different variable from the chronic pre-intervention-vs-post-intervention CMJ height (Table 2 / Tests sheet) that outcome_var=CMJ_mean/time_var=Time/primary_time=post in the registry targets. So even the label 'CMJ' is ambiguous between two different constructs in this paper. (3) Methodologically, even restricting to the intended chronic CMJ height: the authors' deposited R code ('Analyses Chronic.R') shows the actually PUBLISHED CMJ model was fitted on the 'Performance' sheet using ALL 14 assessment occasions (pre-intervention + 12 weekly in-training CMJ recordings + post-intervention) with an AR(1) correlation structure and CMJ baseline as an added covariate (group x time interaction chi2(13) = 32.40, p = 0.002) -- NOT a simple two-timepoint pre/post model. The registry's 'Langformat pre/post' description and the two-row-per-participant 'Tests' sheet (ID, Group, Sex, Time=pre/post, CMJ_mean) reproduce Table 2's descriptive means but do NOT reproduce the model/inferential statistic the paper actually reports for chronic CMJ; a faithful reanalysis of chronic CMJ would need the 14-timepoint 'Performance' sheet, AR(1) structure and baseline covariate, not just sheet 'Tests'. (4) control_arm_matches='yes': TS (traditional/continuous-set training) is consistently treated as the comparator/standard method versus CS (cluster-set training) as the experimental intervention, consistent with registry's arm_control=TS. (5) covars_published='Age,Sex' in the registry only half matches: only Sex is used as a covariate in any published model; Age is never a model covariate (only an eligibility/descriptive variable).

primary_outcome: Whole-body (total) lean body mass, change from baseline
primary_timepoint: Paper does not designate a single primary timepoint; it analyses 3 co-equal stages separately (T1-T2 = post 7-day wash-in; T2-T3 = post 12-week RT; T1-T3 = baseline to post-RT). The result reported first in the Abstract, taken here as the primary contrast per coding rule, is T1-T2 (post 7-day wash-in).
registration_id: ACTRN12622000040763 (Australia New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry)
registry_issues: Our registry.csv row uses data_file 'Desai-Data-LBM-segmental.xlsx' with outcome_var legs_post1/legs_pre (segmental LEG lean mass), with the note 'Ganzkoerper-Magermasse nicht im Deposit, nur Segmente'. This is INCORRECT: whole-body (total) LBM IS present in the deposit, but in the OTHER file, 'Desai-Data-LBM.xlsx' (sheet 'Data'), which has columns dxa_leanmass_kg_pre, dxa_leanmass_kg_post_1, dxa_leanmass_kg_post_2 (and derived lbm_change_post_1/2/3) -- this is exactly the whole-body LBM outcome that the paper actually reports as its main result (Figure 4, Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3). The registry should be updated to point to Desai-Data-LBM.xlsx with outcome_var dxa_leanmass_kg_post_1 (T2, wash-in) or dxa_leanmass_kg_post_2 (T3, post-RT) vs baseline_var dxa_leanmass_kg_pre, rather than the segmental leg columns in Desai-Data-LBM-segmental.xlsx. arm_control='Control' matches the paper's 'Control' group label correctly. Separately: the Abstract states 'Sixty-three... participants were randomised', which equals the n analysed in Table 1 (33 control + 30 supplement), but the Results text separately states 'One male from the CrM group withdrew after the baseline assessment... and was not included in the analysis', implying the true number randomised may have been 64, with the Abstract's '63' actually describing the baseline-analysed sample rather than the randomised sample -- flagged as an internal ambiguity, not resolved here. Also: this trial is described as part of a larger RCT registered under a different title ('The influence of the gut microbiome on resistance training-based skeletal muscle hypertrophy in healthy individuals', ACTRN12622000040763); the registered primary outcome of that larger trial may not be LBM at all -- this could not be verified from the paper text alone (would require checking the ANZCTR entry itself, out of scope here) and is a candidate outcome-switching concern for the reporting audit.

primary_outcome: Psychological General Well-Being Index (PGWBI) global score
primary_timepoint: late pregnancy (gestational week 34-37); also assessed at 3 months postpartum
registry_issues: 1) outcome_var=EPDS_total does NOT match this paper's (abstract-)first-named / most-emphasised outcome: the paper never formally labels a single 'primary outcome' variable for this secondary-analysis report; its abstract heading 'Primary and secondary outcomes measures' actually describes ITT (primary) vs per-protocol (secondary) ANALYSIS POPULATIONS, not an outcome hierarchy. Two outcome domains are named as aims: (a) psychological well-being (PGWBI, late pregnancy and 3-months postpartum) and (b) postnatal depression (EPDS). PGWBI is named first in the Abstract Objectives, described in far greater methodological detail, analysed via a pre-specified baseline-adjusted ANCOVA, and reported first in Results/Discussion; EPDS/postnatal depression is presented as an additional/secondary aim within this paper. We therefore coded PGWBI as the primary outcome per the task's default rule (first-named in abstract), which means outcome_var=EPDS_total in the registry targets what this paper treats as a secondary outcome, not its main one. 2) baseline_var=(empty) for EPDS is actually consistent with the paper: no EPDS baseline mean/SD/n is reported anywhere (Methods, Results, Tables, Figures) for either arm; the only EPDS numbers given are single post-values at 3 months postpartum (exercise 2.96, 95% CI 1.7-4.2; control 3.48, 95% CI 2.3-4.7; p=0.55), compared with a plain independent-samples t-test with NO baseline adjustment ('We analysed differences between groups in EPDS using an independent samples t-test.') - unlike PGWBI, which explicitly uses baseline-adjusted ANCOVA. So the missing EPDS baseline is a genuine feature of the published analysis, not obviously a defect of the Dryad deposit alone - though it is worth confirming whether the deposited dataset even contains an EPDS baseline variable at all. 3) covars_published=Pre_preg_BMI is NOT supported by the paper's statistical methods for either PGWBI or EPDS: prepregnancy BMI is used only as an inclusion criterion / descriptive baseline characteristic, never as a covariate in any reported between-group model (the only covariates used anywhere are the outcome's own prior-timepoint values, for PGWBI only). 4) arm_control=1 cannot be verified from the paper text, which never reports numeric codes for the 'Group' variable; this needs to be checked directly against the Dryad dataset/codebook. 5) Abstract states 'late pregnancy 72 (exercise 38, control 36)' which is arithmetically inconsistent (38+36=74, not 72); Table 2 clearly shows n=38 (exercise) and n=36 (control) analysed for the late-pregnancy PGWBI comparison, so we used 74 for n_analysed_primary. Postpartum numbers (36+34=70) are internally consistent.

primary_outcome: Body weight (kg) — one of three co-primary outcomes (with triceps brachii muscle thickness and push-up endurance)
primary_timepoint: Week 8 (post-intervention), vs. Week 0 baseline
registry_issues: 1) n_arms: the paper has 3 randomised arms (eTRE, dTRE, Control), not the 2 our registry row lists in arm_include. However this does NOT mean the paper only reports an omnibus 3-group test: the primary LMM used dummy-coded Group with Control as the reference category, so the paper explicitly reports a pairwise eTRE-vs-Control contrast (both a post-only simple effect, beta=-2.92, SE=1.00, 95% CI [-4.88,-0.95], p=0.004, and the Time x Group interaction/change-score contrast, beta=2.13, SE=0.48, 95% CI [1.18,3.07], p<0.001) alongside a separate dTRE-vs-Control contrast. Our registry's 2-arm subset (Control vs eTRE) is therefore a legitimate, directly-reported subset of the paper's own primary analysis, not an ad hoc contrast the paper never made. Tukey's HSD post hoc tests were additionally run across all pairwise group x time cells. 2) Body weight is only 1 of 3 co-primary outcomes declared in the Abstract ('The primary outcomes included body weight, the thickness of the triceps brachii long head..., and push-up endurance'); it is listed first among the three and is the outcome most emphasised in the Abstract/Results as the key significant finding, but no formal outcome hierarchy or multiplicity correction across the 3 co-primary outcomes is reported. 3) Deposited data naming mismatch: the Zenodo CSV 'Body data.csv' labels the delayed-TRE arm as 'mTRE', but the paper text (53 occurrences) exclusively calls it 'dTRE' -- the group is never called 'mTRE' anywhere in the manuscript. This does not affect the Control/eTRE contrast our registry uses (those labels match the paper exactly), but it is a genuine data-vs-paper naming discrepancy worth flagging for provenance. 4) Minor: registry id_var is given as 'Participant.ID' (dot) but the actual CSV column header is 'Participant-ID' (hyphen); likely harmless if read with a pipeline that sanitises names (e.g. base R read.csv), but flagged for completeness. 5) Registry outcome_var='Weight', arm_var='Group', time_var='Time', primary_time='post' all match the CSV columns/values exactly for the Control and eTRE rows.

primary_outcome: Sunnybrook Facial Grading System (SFGS) total composite score (comprising resting symmetry, voluntary movement, and synkinesis subscales)
primary_timepoint: Change score from baseline to 20th day (post-intervention, end of 3-week treatment); assessments also taken at baseline and 10th day (mid-intervention)
registration_id: CTRI/2020/02/023240 (paper text renders it as 'CTRI/2020/02/023,240'; the comma is very likely a PDF text-extraction artifact, not part of the actual registry ID)
registry_issues: 1) OUTCOME VARIABLE: The paper's headline/primary result (quoted in the Abstract and matching Table 3 exactly, p = 0.002) is for the SFGS TOTAL COMPOSITE SCORE, baseline-to-20th-day change score - not the voluntary movement (VM) subscore alone. Our registry's outcome_var=VM2 is mismatched on two counts: (a) it targets the VM subscore rather than the composite score the paper's abstract/headline result refers to (the VM subscore's own baseline-to-20th-day change-score p-value in Table 3 is p = 0.013, not p = 0.002); (b) inspection of the deposited 'Data sheet.xlsx' shows VM1/VM2/VM3 correspond to baseline/10th day (mid-intervention)/20th day (post-intervention) respectively - so VM2 is the MID-intervention value, not the final (20th-day) follow-up value used in the paper's primary change-score analysis (which would require VM3). 2) COMPOSITE SCORE AVAILABILITY: Contrary to our prior note ('SFGS-Composite nicht im Datensatz'), the deposited Data sheet.xlsx DOES contain the SFGS total composite score, as columns T1 (baseline)/T2 (10th day)/T3 (20th day) - verified by recomputing group medians from the raw data, which reproduce the published Table 1/Table 2 composite-score medians exactly (e.g., experimental baseline median 31.5, 20th-day median 90.0). So a composite-score re-analysis is in fact possible from the deposited data; the registry should reference T1 (baseline) vs T3 (20th day/final), not VM1/VM2. 3) CONTROL ARM: Cross-checking the deposited dataset's Group/Age/Gender columns against Table 1 shows Group=1 reproduces the EXPERIMENTAL group's reported baseline statistics exactly (median age 39.5 vs Table 1's 39.5; 58.3% male vs Table 1's 58.3%) and Group=2 reproduces the CONVENTIONAL/control group's statistics exactly (median age 45.0; 90.9% male); Group=2 is also the arm containing the single participant lost to follow-up, consistent with the paper's text ('Following allocation to the conventional group... data collection for one patient was incomplete and lost to follow-up'). This means Group=1 = experimental/intervention arm and Group=2 = conventional/control arm - the OPPOSITE of our registry's arm_control=1. 4) COVARIATE: covars_published=Age in our registry does not correspond to an actual adjustment covariate in the paper; Age was used only for a baseline-balance test (Table 1), not in any outcome model (the primary analysis is an unadjusted nonparametric group comparison of change scores).

primary_outcome: Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ) - change from baseline in disability
primary_timepoint: 6 months (= week 26 in the deposited dataset's 'week' variable, which takes values 2, 6, 12, 26 corresponding to the 2-week, 6-week, 3-month and 6-month follow-up occasions; the paper's own text always says '6 months', never literally '26 weeks')
registry_issues: primary_time=26 (Woche) ist KORREKT / BESTAETIGT, war aber in registry.csv nur 'ANGENOMMEN': Das Paper selbst spricht im Fliesstext nur von '6 months' (nie woertlich '26 weeks'), aber die deponierten Datensaetze (FREE_Patient_Outcome_Data_v1_0.csv) enthalten eine Variable 'week' mit genau den vier Werten {2, 6, 12, 26}, entsprechend den vier Follow-up-Zeitpunkten (2 Wochen, 6 Wochen, 3 Monate, 6 Monate); week=26 entspricht damit eindeutig dem primaeren 6-Monats-Zeitpunkt. outcome_var=rmdq_tot und baseline_var=rmdq_tot_base sind KORREKT (passen exakt zur Data Dictionary: 'rmdq_tot' = RMDQ-Summenscore beim Follow-up, 'rmdq_tot_base' = RMDQ-Summenscore bei Baseline; RMDQ ist laut Methods-Abschnitt 'Outcomes' explizit das 'primary patient-level outcome'). arm_var=Tment mit Werten 'FREE'/'Control' ist KORREKT bestaetigt (direkt im Datensatz geprueft), arm_control='Control' ist KORREKT. cluster_vars=practice_code ist NUR TEILWEISE korrekt: 'practice_code' entspricht der tatsaechlich randomisierten Einheit (8 Praxen, cluster-randomisiert stratifiziert nach Praxisgroesse), ABER das publizierte Primaermodell modelliert die Clusterung von Patientenoutcomes NICHT ueber practice_code, sondern ueber einen GP-Random-Effekt (Random Intercept + Slope fuer den einzelnen Hausarzt/die Hausaerztin, Spalte 'GP' im Datensatz): 'for patient outcomes by specifying random effects for the GP ... whereas randomisation was at the practice level, clustering effects on outcome values were expected to be mostly driven by interpractitioner variability' (Statistical analysis, p. 7/20). Eine originalgetreue Reanalyse sollte daher nach GP clustern (nicht nach practice_code) und zusaetzlich die Praxisgroessen-Stratifizierungsvariable (pracsize_strata, <=8 vs. >8 FTE GPs) als fixen Kovariaten-Term aufnehmen. covars_published und strat_vars sind in registry.csv LEER/nicht befuellt; sollten laut Paper ergaenzt werden um: covars_published = baseline RMDQ, age, gender, NZDep, back pain duration, back pain nature (constant/episodic), recent/ongoing non-GP healthcare use, previous back pain history, baseline psychosocial factors (PSEQ-2, recovery expectations), GP-level baseline HC-PAIRS; strat_vars = pracsize_strata. published_est/published_p sind in registry.csv leer; sollten mit 0.57 (95% CI -0.64 bis 1.78) und p=0.354 befuellt werden.

primary_outcome: Muscle thickness (hypertrophy) of the quadriceps femoris (rectus femoris and vastus lateralis, measured at 30/50/70% femur length) and triceps surae (medial/lateral gastrocnemius, soleus), assessed by B-mode ultrasound. This is the first-named outcome domain in the Abstract ('Muscle growth outcomes included assessments of muscle thickness...'); the paper never uses the word 'primary' or 'co-primary' anywhere in the text, and treats 9 muscle-thickness/body-composition sites as statistically co-equal (Table 2). Rectus femoris 50% (registry outcome_var) is one of these 9 sites.
primary_timepoint: Post-intervention (end of 9-week training block, ultrasound taken >=48h after the last training session) vs. baseline (Pre); single pre-post comparison, no intermediate muscle-thickness timepoint
registration_id: OSF preregistration https://osf.io/bztka (methods preregistered prior to recruitment); data/materials at https://osf.io/kdgv3 (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/KDGV3)
registry_issues: 1) No declared primary outcome: the word 'primary' (or 'co-primary') does not occur anywhere in the paper. The registry note 'Muskeldicke koprimaer an mehreren Stellen' is a reasonable inference from the symmetric treatment of 9 muscle-thickness/body-composition outcomes in Table 2, but is not the authors' own language. RF50 (Rectus femoris 50%) is one of these 9 co-equal sites; it is somewhat more prominent than RF30/RF70/VL30/VL70/lateral gastrocnemius/soleus because it is one of only 3 sites (RF50, VL50, medial gastrocnemius) entered into the multivariate composite model, but the paper never singles it out as THE primary outcome. 2) arm_control mismatch: registry.csv codes arm_control='1', but checking the raw deposited dataset (Dataset Deload.xlsx, GROUP column) against Table 1 descriptive stats shows GROUP=1 has n=18 with RF50 Pre/Post means 41.4/45.5 mm, which matches the DELOAD arm (n=18) in Table 1 -- i.e. GROUP=1 is DELOAD, the intervention/experimental arm, not the control. GROUP=2 (n=21, RF50 Pre/Post 44.7/49.3 mm) matches TRAD (n=21), which the paper itself treats as the de facto control/reference arm (Fig. 2/3 captions: 'Negative values favor control and positive values favor the inclusion of a detraining period'; Limitations: 'the TRAD condition (which essentially served as a control)'). So the registry's arm_control value ('1') is coded to the wrong group; the true control arm is GROUP=2 (TRAD). 3) covars_published=SEX in registry does not match the paper: the Statistical analyses section lists no covariates (only 'group' and repeated-measures/time terms) for the primary group-difference models; sex is reported only descriptively, not as an adjustment covariate.

primary_outcome: Muscle thickness (hypertrophy) of the elbow flexors and elbow extensors, assessed via B-mode ultrasonography at 45% and 55% of humeral length - the first-named outcome domain in the abstract (named before strength-endurance). The paper reports four parallel muscle-thickness sites (elbow flexor 45%, elbow flexor 55%, elbow extensor 45%, elbow extensor 55%) with no single site singled out as primary; the site coded as outcome_var in our registry (BB55) corresponds to elbow flexor / biceps brachii thickness at 55% of humeral length, one of these four sites.
primary_timepoint: Post-intervention (after the 8-week resistance-training program) vs. pre-intervention baseline; only two timepoints (pre, post) were assessed
registration_id: OSF preregistration https://osf.io/86v2h (registered prior to data collection); data/materials deposited at https://osf.io/a6cpz, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/A6CPZ
registry_issues: (1) Studiendesign ist kein klassisches 2-Arm-Parallelgruppen-RCT, sondern ein Innerhalb-Person/kontralaterale-Extremitaet-Vergleich: 30 randomisierte Teilnehmer, deren zwei Arme je einer von zwei Trainingsbedingungen (pROM/fROM) zugelost wurden; jede Person liefert Daten zu beiden Bedingungen. 'arm_control'/'Kontrollarm' im klassischen Sinn existiert nicht - beide Bedingungen sind aktive Trainingsinterventionen. registry arm_control=1 (=pROM) ist nur eine Referenzcodierung fuer die Reanalyse, keine echte Kontrollgruppe -> control_arm_matches = 'no'. (2) Kein im Paper formal deklariertes primaeres Outcome (bestaetigt Registry-Notiz): vier Muskeldicke-Messorte (Ellbogenflexor 45%/55%, Ellbogenextensor 45%/55%) und zwei Kraft-Ausdauer-Messungen (10RM voll/partiell) werden als gleichrangige Co-Outcomes mit separaten Bayes-Faktoren berichtet (Tabelle 4). (3) Registry-outcome_var BB55 (Bizeps/Ellbogenflexor bei 55% Humeruslaenge) ist plausibel dem im Abstract zuerst genannten Outcome-Bereich (Muskeldicke, vor Kraft-Ausdauer genannt) zuzuordnen, aber im Abstract/Methodentext werden 45% und 55% stets gemeinsam und ohne Praeferenz genannt (45% wird textuell sogar zuerst erwaehnt) und Flexor/Extensor werden ebenfalls gemeinsam genannt -> outcome_var_matches_primary = 'unclear'. (4) n_randomised=30 und n_analysed=25 (5 Dropouts) stimmen mit den Rohdaten ueberein: 'Data Sheet.xlsx', Sheet 'Muscle Thickness', 25 Zeilen mit GROUP=1 und 25 Zeilen mit GROUP=2 fuer BB55. (5) Legendenzeilen ('1 = pROM', '2 = fROM') wurden am Ende der GROUP-Spalte in der Rohdatei bestaetigt; arm_include='1,2' filtert diese korrekt heraus. (6) primary_time/covars_published/strat_vars/cluster_vars/published_est/published_p sind in der Registry-Zeile leer - konsistent mit fehlender formaler Primaeranalyse-Deklaration im Paper; die in dieser JSON dokumentierten Schaetzer stammen direkt aus Tabelle 4 des Papers.

primary_outcome: Self-reported physical activity level (Godin-Shephard Leisure-Time Exercise Questionnaire, LTPA-Q)
primary_timepoint: T1 = immediately post-intervention (end of the 12-week Lymfit program / end of 12-week wait period for controls)
registry_issues: (1) This is a pilot/feasibility RCT: the paper's actual stated primary aim is feasibility (a priori benchmarks for recruitment, retention, questionnaire completion, fidelity, missing data, Fitbit adherence, control-group design - all met), with acceptability as a second aim. There is no single outcome formally labelled 'primary outcome' for efficacy. The Methods/Objectives section lists 'preliminary effects on four study outcomes' as one aim, in the order: psychological need satisfaction (PNSE), exercise motivation (BREQ-3), physical activity level (Godin/LTPA-Q, our POST_Godin), and health-related quality of life (PROPr) - i.e. Godin/LTPA-Q is listed THIRD of four in Methods, not first. The Abstract, however, first names 'self-reported physical activity levels' among the ANCOVA findings, which is why this extraction used the abstract rule and picked LTPA-Q/POST_Godin as 'primary_outcome_name'. Because no true single primary outcome is declared anywhere, outcome_var_matches_primary is coded 'unclear' rather than 'yes'. (2) Covariate mismatch: our registry line lists covars_published='Age,BMI', but the paper's ANCOVA models adjust ONLY for the outcome's own baseline (T0) value, not for Age or BMI (these appear only in the descriptive Table 1, with a note of no significant baseline group differences). This should be corrected/flagged in the registry. (3) Minor numeric inconsistency in the paper itself: abstract reports mean age 32.1 years vs. Results/Table 1 reporting 32.35/32.4 years (SD 5.82) - not related to our registry, noted for completeness.

primary_outcome: NPRS-Lumbar Pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, lumbar back pain)
primary_timepoint: Week 3 (post-intervention, after 10 treatment sessions over three weeks), compared with baseline (pre-intervention)
journal: Medicina (MDPI, published on behalf of Lithuanian University of Health Sciences); Medicina 2026, 62, 249; https://doi.org/10.3390/medicina62020249
registry_issues: (1) ARM CODING MISMATCH: registry.csv lists arm_control=1, but the deposited SPSS file (Lytras FMS 1 data.sav) defines GROUP value labels as 1.0 = 'Manual Therapy with FMS' (the intervention arm) and 2.0 = 'Manual therpay alone' (the actual control arm). So the control arm is GROUP=2, not GROUP=1 as currently coded in the registry -- this needs correction. (2) COVARIATE MISMATCH: registry.csv lists covars_published='Age,Gender,BMI', but the paper's published primary analysis (two-way mixed ANOVA with only 'group' and 'time' factors) does not adjust for Age, Gender/Sex or BMI (or any other covariate) at all. These three variables (plus symptom duration, affected side, herniation level) are used only for a descriptive baseline-balance comparison in Table 2 (independent t-tests / chi-square), not as model covariates for the primary outcome. B_covariates is therefore coded 'none', not 'published_set'. (3) OUTCOME VAR MATCH CONFIRMED: outcome_var=NRPSLBPpost / baseline_var=NRPSLBPpre correspond to 'NPRS lumbar pain 3rd week' / 'NPRS lumbar pain baseline' in the SPSS labels, which matches the paper's NPRS-Lumbar Pain outcome -- this is one of the co-primary outcomes both in the paper (Methods 2.4: 'All outcomes were considered primary') and in the ClinicalTrials.gov registration NCT07234071 (which lists 'Pain Intensity (NPRS)', 'Straight Leg Raise (SLR) Angle', 'Change in Functional Disability' [RMDQ], and 'Change in Neuropathic Symptom Profile' [S-LANSS] as four co-equal Primary Outcome Measures, with NPRS listed first and covering both lumbar and leg pain). No single outcome is hierarchically primary; NPRS-Lumbar is the first-named/first-discussed of the pain measures in both the registration order and the paper's own subsection order (2.4.1), consistent with the registry's prior choice. (4) The task prompt's working hypothesis that 'FMS' might refer to 'Functional Movement Screen' (suggested by the title wording given in the task) is incorrect for this paper: FMS here stands for 'Functional Magnetic Stimulation', a magnetic-field neuromodulation device applied concurrently with manual therapy -- it is a treatment component/co-intervention, not an outcome measure and not related to the Functional Movement Screen assessment tool.

primary_outcome: Postpartum depression, assessed with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) total score and the dichotomised risk-of-depression category (EPDS>10), at 1 month postpartum. primary_timepoint: Nicht deklariert. Das Paper schaetzt 5 separate Netzwerke (baseline, 5, 10, 26, 52 Wochen) parallel, ohne einen Zeitpunkt als primaer zu benennen. Woche 26 ist lediglich die von unserer Registry gewaehlte Konvention (primary_time=26), nicht eine Angabe des Papers selbst.
registry_issues: Q1 (Pain intensity) ist im Paper NICHT als primaeres Outcome deklariert. Das Paper behandelt alle 10 ODI-Items (Q1-Q10) gleichrangig als Netzwerk-Knoten; es gibt keine Hierarchie, die Q1 hervorhebt. In den Ergebnissen werden zwar Sleep (Q7) und Pain (Q1) als die Items genannt, die konsistent ueber alle Follow-ups mit der Gruppe assoziiert sind, und Pain/Social life/Work als die zentralsten Knoten -- aber das ist ein deskriptives Ergebnis der Netzwerkanalyse, keine a priori Festlegung von Q1 als primaerem Outcome. Der eigentliche 'primaere Endpunkt' der zugrunde liegenden STOPS-RCT (registriert unter ACTRN12609000834257) ist in diesem Paper nicht genannt/nicht reproduziert -- dafuer muesste der originaere Trial-Bericht (Ref. [32] Ford et al.; Ref. [34] Hahne et al., Protokoll) herangezogen werden, der hier nicht extrahiert wurde. Das Paper selbst bestaetigt indirekt, dass im originaeren RCT ein Gesamt-/Aggregatscore-Outcome verwendet wurde: 'the overall outcomes for pain (5, 10 & 26 weeks) and function (10, 26 and 52 weeks) favoured the IP group in the RCT [32]' (p. 12/17) -- 'function' duerfte sich auf den ODI-Gesamtscore beziehen, der hier NICHT gebildet/analysiert wird ('We treated the items of the ODI as continuous variables' statt eines Summenscores, p. 6/17). Damit ist Q1 als 'Platzhalter fuers primaere Outcome' in unserer Registry problematisch: Q1 ist real im Paper vorhanden und sogar unter den zwei am konsistentesten von der Gruppe beeinflussten Items, aber es ist explizit NICHT das primaere/einzige Zielkriterium, und eine Summenbildung zum ODI-Gesamtscore (wie es der originaere Trial vermutlich nutzte) waere -- wie in der Registry-Notiz korrekt antizipiert -- eine eigene, im Deposit/Paper nicht vorgenommene Analyseentscheidung. arm_control='adv' (Advice) passt korrekt zum im Paper beschriebenen 'Advice'-Arm (guideline-based advice, 2x30-min Sitzungen, Group=0); der Interventionsarm ist 'Individualised Physiotherapy' (Group=1). primary_time=26 (Woche 26) ist ein Registry-Konventionswert; das Paper selbst weist keinem der 5 Zeitpunkte (baseline, 5, 10, 26, 52 Wochen) Primaeritaet zu. Bei Woche 26 betraegt die vollstaendige Fallzahl (complete case) n=271, was zu 'n_analysed_primary' in dieser Extraktion passt, aber ebenfalls nur eine von 5 parallelen, gleichrangigen Analysen ist.

registry_issues: AP_RMS is NOT the primary outcome of the underlying trial. The paper explicitly states: 'The primary outcomes of the trial itself were fall risk, dynamic balance, and physical activity levels, whereas the secondary outcomes were fall risk appraisal (comprising level of fear for falling and static balance performance) and negative self-perceptions of aging. In this exploratory analysis, the static balance of older adults was focused on...' This paper is explicitly labelled an 'exploratory analysis' of static balance (a sub-component of a secondary trial outcome), reporting four static balance metrics (AP RMS, ML RMS, sway speed variability, sway area) in parallel with no stated hierarchy/primary designation among them and no multiplicity correction across the resulting 4 outcomes x 3 time contrasts. AP RMS was chosen as 'the' outcome for our registry only because it is listed first in the Abstract's outcome list ('AP RMS, ML RMS, sway speed variability, and sway area') and in the Statistical Analysis section and Tables 3/4 order; however, the Introduction's closing paragraph lists the metrics in a different order ('sway area, AP root mean square (RMS), ML RMS, and COP sway speed variability'), i.e. sway area first -- so 'first-named outcome' is ambiguous depending on section. Notably, AP RMS shows no significant Group main effect (p=0.667) nor any significant Group*Time interaction at T2/T3/T4 (p=0.389/0.915/0.678); the paper's own emphasized findings are for sway area (marginal Group*Time(T2), Std beta=-0.07, p=0.050) and sway speed variability (significant Group*Time(T4), Std beta=0.10, p=0.014) -- i.e. not for AP RMS at all. Also, the observed statistical power for the AP RMS model is reported as only 22%, flagged by the authors themselves as a reason for caution. Primary_time=4 (T4) is not explicitly declared 'the' primary timepoint by the paper either; both short-term (T1-T2) and medium-term (T1-T4) effects are examined without hierarchy, though the registry's chosen contrast (Group*Time(T4) for AP RMS, raw/log-scale Estimate 0.02, p=0.678) matches Table 3 exactly, confirming which cell of the table the registry pulled from. Covariates (Age, BMI, Gender/Sex, Race) and cluster variable (Site) match the paper exactly (random effects for Subject ID and Site; fixed effects incl. age, BMI, sex, race/ethnicity). Control arm (educational CDC flyers, 'live their lives normally') matches. Time variable (T1-T4 long format) matches.

registry_issues: TWO separate mismatches identified. (1) OUTCOME-SWITCHING (registration vs. publication), explicitly disclosed by the authors themselves: 'At the time of registration, only 5 participants had completed the primary outcome assessment, which was originally cardiorespiratory fitness following the intervention as mentioned in the original protocol. However, cardiorespiratory testing in pregnant women with obesity raised feasibility issues, especially at 28 weeks, and accordingly the primary outcome was modified for the impact of the intervention on physical activity levels, in accordance with the registered protocol...' (Study design, p. 2-3). So the ORIGINAL protocol's primary outcome (cardiorespiratory fitness / VO2 at anaerobic threshold) was replaced, before/at registration, by a physical-activity primary outcome -- consistent with our registry note. (2) WITHIN the 'physical activity' domain, the registry's chosen analysis variable (Steps_per_day) is itself NOT the paper's designated primary outcome. The Methods explicitly state: 'The primary outcome was defined as the time spent at moderate and vigorous physical activity (MVPA) at 36 weeks of gestation' (Outcomes assessment, p. 4), and the a priori sample-size calculation (n=21/group) was powered specifically for this MVPA-in-bouts measure. Furthermore, steps/day shows a WEAKER, non-significant between-group result (36-week between-group comparison p=0.072, i.e. only a trend) compared with the true primary outcome MVPA (significant group main effect p=0.014), so choosing steps/day instead of MVPA also changes the substantive headline finding that would be reanalysed. control_arm_matches is coded 'unclear' because paper.txt does not state the numeric coding of the 'Category' variable (exercise=?, control=?) used in the deposited Dryad_data.xlsx; this can only be verified by inspecting the deposited dataset directly, which was outside the scope of this paper-text-only extraction.
